items.statement: Conformational optical response of the single arm
items.expected: Explain the change in the principal low-energy absorption when the complete neutral-singlet C26H27NO3 single-arm model changes from transoid to cisoid geometry. Use actual gas-phase vertical S0-to-S1 transition energies, oscillator strengths and corresponding physical-state evidence for both candidates. The reference cisoid response is red-shifted and weaker, consistent with changed conjugated-arm geometry; neither the source energy shift nor either energy/strength is a target. Establish which transition is being compared, its molecular origin and whether the geometry is conditional or freely stable. A supported model-sensitive alternative can pass if actual comparable states, geometry and response evidence explain the revised optical conclusion. Source sample labels, two copied scalars, or a frozen torsion presented as a populated free minimum fail. This item concerns the one-arm response, not the full dye or the identity of the 700 nm band.

items.statement: Conformational redistribution of the full-dye absorption
items.expected: Determine how transoid/cisoid arm arrangement changes the low-energy absorption pattern of the full neutral-singlet C66H69N3O3 chromophore. Report the actual S1-S4 energies and oscillator strengths at both declared S0 gas-phase geometries and interpret their physical-state correspondence and redistribution of intensity. Reference spectra retain two bright low states and much weaker higher states, with a modest cisoid redshift and a redistribution between the two bright transitions. Score the supported spectral conclusion rather than an exact eight-state matrix: no source energies, strengths, dark-root order or fixed configuration percentage is required to match. A changed state ordering or mixing is acceptable when actual response evidence establishes which states exchange character and explains the resulting spectrum. Distinguish a constrained cisoid candidate from an unconstrained minimum; this spectral calculation does not itself establish solution populations or a photoproduct.

Explain which single-arm findings transfer to the full three-arm chromophore and which do not, using actual comparative spectral and transition-density/orbital evidence. The conformational redshift tendency transfers, while the full dye has two low bright states with coupled/mixed arm response instead of a single isolated-arm excitation; higher states are much weaker. Exact canonical orbital indices or printed configuration percentages are not required. This is a physical account of model reduction, not another point for the same redshift sign or a generic limitations paragraph.

Use actual conformer-resolved absorption calculations and state correspondence to explain a cisoid redshift as a possible molecular contribution to the extra long-wavelength feature. Compare the calculated transition energies to the approximately 700 nm observation: this finite gas-phase conformer model does not quantitatively reproduce that band or uniquely establish its photoproduct. Explain the physical limits of this inference and distinguish a conditional twisted geometry from a thermally populated free minimum. A raw redshift list or repetition of the observed band does not pass; genuine alternative physically equivalent analyses can pass.
